questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In diploblastic animals, an undifferentiated layer called mesoglea is present between the ectoderm and the endoderm.
Statement II: Coelenterates and ctenophores are diploblastic animals.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: animals whose cells are arranged in two embryonic layers, an external ectoderm and an internal endoderm, are diploblastic, e.g. coelenterates; an undifferentiated layer, mesoglea, is present between them. Ctenophores too are described as diploblastic. Animals with a third (middle) layer, the mesoderm, are triploblastic (platyhelminthes to chordates).
steps: Statement I: mesoglea lies between ectoderm and endoderm → true
Statement II: coelenterates and ctenophores are diploblastic → true
solution.why_others_wrong: Both statements are NCERT lines, so any option calling one of them false is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Animal Kingdom', basis of classification: diploblastic and triploblastic organisation
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: An animal is triploblastic and bilaterally symmetrical, and has a complete alimentary canal with a muscular pharynx. Its body cavity is not lined by mesoderm; instead, the mesoderm is present as scattered pouches between the ectoderm and the endoderm. The animal belongs to the phylum:

options.text: Platyhelminthes
Annelida
Aschelminthes
Ctenophora

solution.explanation: A body cavity not lined by mesoderm, with mesoderm in scattered pouches, is a pseudocoelom; such animals are pseudocoelomates, e.g. aschelminthes. Aschelminthes are also triploblastic, bilaterally symmetrical and have a complete alimentary canal with a well-developed muscular pharynx. Flatworms are acoelomate with an incomplete gut; annelids are coelomates; ctenophores are diploblastic.
steps: Pseudocoelomate + complete gut with muscular pharynx → Aschelminthes
solution.why_others_wrong: Platyhelminthes have no body cavity and an incomplete digestive system; Annelida have a true coelom; Ctenophora are diploblastic.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Animal Kingdom', basis of classification: coelom; phylum Aschelminthes
solution.final_answer: Option C: Aschelminthes

Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Animals generally show locomotion in search of food, shelter, a mate, suitable breeding grounds or favourable climatic conditions, or to escape from enemies or predators.
Reason (R): Methods of locomotion performed by animals vary with their habitats and the demand of the situation.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: methods of locomotion performed by animals vary with their habitats and the demand of the situation. However, locomotion is generally for search of food, shelter, mate, suitable breeding grounds, favourable climatic conditions or to escape from enemies/predators. R explains how locomotion varies, not why animals move about, so it is not the explanation of A.
steps: R explains the variety of methods, not the purpose → not the explanation
solution.why_others_wrong: A treats the variety of methods as the reason for locomotion; C and D call a true statement false.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Locomotion and Movement', introduction
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the three types of muscles are correct?

(a) Visceral muscles are located in the inner walls of hollow visceral organs such as the alimentary canal and the reproductive tract.
(b) Visceral muscles are non-striated and involuntary.
(c) Cardiac muscle fibres are striated and involuntary.
(d) Skeletal muscle fibres are non-striated.
(e) Muscles contribute about 70–80 per cent of the body weight of a human adult.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: (a), (c) and (e) only
(b), (c) and (d) only
(a), (b) and (c) only
(a), (b), (d) and (e) only

solution.explanation: NCERT: skeletal muscles are closely associated with skeletal components and are striated and voluntary. Visceral muscles lie in the inner walls of hollow visceral organs such as the alimentary canal and reproductive tract; they are smooth (non-striated) and involuntary. Cardiac muscles are striated and involuntary. Muscles contribute about 40–50 per cent of the body weight of a human adult.
solution.why_others_wrong: A includes (e); B includes (d); D includes (d) and (e).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Locomotion and Movement', muscle
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A motor neuron stimulates a skeletal muscle fibre and an action potential spreads through it, but a drug blocks the release of Ca²⁺ from the sarcoplasmic reticulum. What will happen?

options.text: Myosin heads will bind actin permanently, and the fibre will stay contracted
Acetylcholine will not be released at the neuromuscular junction
The A-bands will shorten while the I-bands stay unchanged
Troponin will continue to mask the active sites on actin, so cross bridges cannot form and the fibre will not contract

solution.concept: Role of calcium in muscle contraction
solution.explanation: NCERT: the action potential in the sarcolemma causes the release of Ca²⁺ into the sarcoplasm. Ca²⁺ binds to a subunit of troponin on the actin filaments and removes the masking of the active sites for myosin; only then can the myosin head bind actin to form a cross bridge. Without Ca²⁺ release the active sites stay masked and no contraction occurs.
steps: Action potential → Ca²⁺ release from sarcoplasmic reticulum
No Ca²⁺ → sites stay masked → no cross bridge → no contraction
solution.why_others_wrong: Cross bridges cannot form at all without Ca²⁺; acetylcholine release happens earlier at the nerve ending and is unaffected; A-bands never shorten during contraction.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Locomotion and Movement', mechanism of muscle contraction
solution.final_answer: Option D: Troponin will continue to mask the active sites on actin, so cross bridges cannot form and the fibre will not contract

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Flagellar movement helps in the swimming of spermatozoa, maintenance of the water current in the canal system of sponges and locomotion of protozoans like Euglena.
Statement II: Amoeboid movement is brought about by flagella.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: flagellar movement helps in the swimming of spermatozoa, maintenance of water current in the canal system of sponges and locomotion of protozoans like Euglena. Amoeboid movement is effected by pseudopodia formed by the streaming of protoplasm (as in Amoeba); cytoskeletal elements like microfilaments are also involved. Flagella do not cause amoeboid movement.
steps: Statement II: amoeboid movement is by pseudopodia → false
solution.why_others_wrong: A and D accept the false Statement II; B rejects the true Statement I.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Locomotion and Movement', types of movement
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A nerve impulse is transmitted from one neuron to another through junctions called:

options.text: Nodes of Ranvier
Neuromuscular junctions
Synapses
Nissl's granules

solution.explanation: NCERT: a nerve impulse is transmitted from one neuron to another through junctions called synapses. Nodes of Ranvier are gaps between adjacent myelin sheaths, a neuromuscular junction links a motor neuron to a muscle fibre, and Nissl's granules are granular bodies in the cell body.
solution.why_others_wrong: Nodes of Ranvier lie along one fibre; a neuromuscular junction links a neuron to a muscle; Nissl's granules are not junctions.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Neural Control and Coordination', generation and conduction of nerve impulse: transmission of impulses
solution.final_answer: Option C: Synapses

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In the human forebrain, the cerebrum wraps around a structure called the:

options.text: Medulla oblongata
Cerebellum
Pons
Thalamus

solution.explanation: NCERT: the forebrain consists of the cerebrum, thalamus and hypothalamus. The cerebrum wraps around a structure called the thalamus, which is a major coordinating centre for sensory and motor signalling.
solution.why_others_wrong: The medulla, cerebellum and pons are parts of the hindbrain, not wrapped by the cerebrum.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Neural Control and Coordination', central neural system: forebrain
solution.final_answer: Option D: Thalamus

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The cerebellum has a very convoluted surface. This:

options.text: Reduces the number of neurons it contains
Provides additional space for many more neurons
Allows the cerebellum to secrete hypothalamic hormones
Connects the two cerebral hemispheres

solution.explanation: NCERT: the cerebellum has a very convoluted surface in order to provide the additional space for many more neurons.
steps: Convoluted surface → more area → space for many more neurons
solution.why_others_wrong: The folding increases, not decreases, room for neurons; hypothalamic hormones come from the hypothalamus; the corpus callosum connects the hemispheres.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Neural Control and Coordination', central neural system: hindbrain
solution.final_answer: Option B: Provides additional space for many more neurons

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (neuron or nerve fibre) with List-II (where commonly found).

List-I:
A. Multipolar neurons
B. Bipolar neurons
C. Myelinated nerve fibres
D. Unmyelinated nerve fibres

List-II:
I. Autonomous and somatic neural systems
II. Spinal and cranial nerves
III. Retina of the eye
IV. Cerebral cortex

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I
A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II
A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I
A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I

solution.concept: Types of neurons and nerve fibres
solution.explanation: NCERT: multipolar neurons (one axon, two or more dendrites) are found in the cerebral cortex; bipolar neurons (one axon, one dendrite) in the retina of the eye. Myelinated nerve fibres are found in spinal and cranial nerves; unmyelinated fibres are commonly found in the autonomous and the somatic neural systems.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other codes swap the multipolar and bipolar sites, the myelinated and unmyelinated sites, or multipolar neurons with myelinated fibres.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Neural Control and Coordination', neuron as structural and functional unit of neural system
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The inner parts of the cerebral hemispheres and a group of associated deep structures form a complex structure called the limbic lobe or limbic system. These deep structures include:

options.text: Pons and medulla
Corpora quadrigemina
Corpus callosum and cerebral aqueduct
Amygdala and hippocampus

solution.explanation: NCERT: the inner parts of the cerebral hemispheres and a group of associated deep structures like the amygdala, hippocampus, etc. form the limbic lobe or limbic system. Along with the hypothalamus, it is involved in the regulation of sexual behaviour, expression of emotional reactions and motivation.
steps: Limbic system → inner cerebral hemispheres + amygdala, hippocampus, etc.
solution.why_others_wrong: The pons and medulla are hindbrain; corpora quadrigemina and the cerebral aqueduct belong to the midbrain; the corpus callosum is a fibre tract joining the hemispheres.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Neural Control and Coordination', central neural system: forebrain
solution.final_answer: Option D: Amygdala and hippocampus

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The medulla oblongata is a part of the forebrain.
Reason (R): The medulla of the brain is connected to the spinal cord.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: the hindbrain comprises the pons, cerebellum and medulla (also called the medulla oblongata). The medulla of the brain is connected to the spinal cord. A places the medulla in the forebrain, so A is false; R is true.
steps: Medulla connected to spinal cord → R true
solution.why_others_wrong: A, B and C accept the false assertion.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Neural Control and Coordination', central neural system: hindbrain
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: A synapse is formed by the membranes of a pre-synaptic neuron and a post-synaptic neuron, which may or may not be separated by a gap called the synaptic cleft.
Statement II: At a chemical synapse, neurotransmitters are released by the post-synaptic neuron and act on receptors of the pre-synaptic membrane.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: a synapse is formed by the membranes of a pre-synaptic neuron and a post-synaptic neuron, which may or may not be separated by a gap called the synaptic cleft. At a chemical synapse, the synaptic vesicles of the axon terminal (pre-synaptic side) release neurotransmitters into the cleft, and these bind to specific receptors on the post-synaptic membrane. Statement II reverses the direction.
steps: Statement II: release is pre-synaptic, receptors are post-synaptic → false
solution.why_others_wrong: A and D accept the reversed Statement II; B rejects the true Statement I.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Neural Control and Coordination', transmission of impulses
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the structure of a neuron are correct?

(a) A neuron is a microscopic structure composed of three major parts: the cell body, dendrites and axon.
(b) Axons transmit nerve impulses away from the cell body to a synapse or to a neuromuscular junction.
(c) The cell body of a neuron lacks typical cell organelles.
(d) Each branch of the axon terminates as a bulb-like structure called a synaptic knob.
(e) Dendrites transmit impulses away from the cell body.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: (a), (c) and (d) only
(a), (b) and (d) only
(b), (d) and (e) only
(a), (b), (c) and (e) only

solution.explanation: NCERT: a neuron is a microscopic structure composed of three major parts: cell body, dendrites and axon. The cell body contains cytoplasm with typical cell organelles and Nissl's granules. Dendrites transmit impulses towards the cell body; the axon transmits impulses away from the cell body to a synapse or a neuromuscular junction. The distal end of the axon is branched, and each branch terminates as a bulb-like synaptic knob.
steps: (e) False: dendrites carry impulses towards the cell body
solution.why_others_wrong: A includes (c); C and D include (e).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Neural Control and Coordination', neuron as structural and functional unit of neural system
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b) and (d) only

questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the human brain are correct?

(a) The brain is the central information processing organ of the body and acts as the 'command and control system'.
(b) The human brain is well protected by the skull.
(c) The forebrain consists of the cerebrum, thalamus and medulla oblongata.
(d) The brain stem is formed by the cerebrum, pons and medulla oblongata.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: (a), (b) and (c) only
(b), (c) and (d) only
(a) and (b) only
(a) and (d) only

solution.explanation: NCERT: the brain is the central information processing organ of our body and acts as the 'command and control system'. The human brain is well protected by the skull. The forebrain consists of the cerebrum, thalamus and hypothalamus; the midbrain, pons and medulla oblongata form the brain stem.
solution.why_others_wrong: A, B and D include the false (c) or (d).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Neural Control and Coordination', central neural system
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a) and (b) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In a resting neuron, the axoplasm has a high K⁺ and low Na⁺ concentration, while the outside fluid has a low K⁺ and high Na⁺ concentration. If the sodium-potassium pump of the axonal membrane were blocked, which would be the most direct consequence?

options.text: The membrane would become freely permeable to the negatively charged proteins of the axoplasm
Na⁺ would start being pumped into the axoplasm in exchange for K⁺
More K⁺ would be pumped in, making the inside of the membrane more negative
These ionic gradients across the resting membrane would no longer be maintained

solution.explanation: NCERT: the ionic gradients across the resting membrane are maintained by the active transport of ions by the sodium-potassium pump, which transports 3 Na⁺ outwards for 2 K⁺ into the cell. If the pump is blocked, the gradients it maintains can no longer be kept up.
steps: Gradients are maintained by active transport through the Na⁺–K⁺ pump
solution.why_others_wrong: The membrane stays impermeable to the axoplasmic proteins; a blocked pump transports nothing, so it neither reverses nor speeds up.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Neural Control and Coordination', generation and conduction of nerve impulse
solution.final_answer: Option D: These ionic gradients across the resting membrane would no longer be maintained

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): When a stimulus is applied at a site on a polarised axonal membrane, the inner surface of the membrane at that site becomes positively charged with respect to the outer surface.
Reason (R): At the site of stimulation, the membrane becomes freely permeable to Na⁺, which leads to a rapid influx of Na⁺.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: when a stimulus is applied at a site on the polarised membrane, the membrane at that site becomes freely permeable to Na⁺. This leads to a rapid influx of Na⁺ followed by the reversal of the polarity at that site: the outer surface becomes negatively charged and the inner side positively charged. The Na⁺ influx causes the reversal, so R explains A.
steps: Na⁺ influx → inside becomes positive → R explains A
solution.why_others_wrong: B ignores the causal sequence NCERT gives; C and D call a true statement false.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Neural Control and Coordination', generation and conduction of nerve impulse
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The autonomic neural system relays impulses from the CNS to the involuntary organs and the smooth muscles of the body.
Statement II: The peripheral neural system is divided into two divisions: the somatic neural system and the autonomic neural system.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: the PNS is divided into the somatic neural system and the autonomic neural system. The somatic system relays impulses from the CNS to the skeletal muscles, while the autonomic system transmits impulses from the CNS to the involuntary organs and smooth muscles of the body. The autonomic system is further divided into sympathetic and parasympathetic systems.
solution.why_others_wrong: Both statements are true, so B, C and D are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Neural Control and Coordination', human neural system
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: At a chemical synapse, a drug blocks the specific receptors on the post-synaptic membrane. An impulse arriving at the axon terminal still causes neurotransmitters to be released into the synaptic cleft. What will follow?

options.text: The neurotransmitters cannot bind and open ion channels, so no new potential is generated in the post-synaptic neuron
The impulse will cross the cleft as an electrical current instead
The pre-synaptic neuron will stop being excitable
The post-synaptic neuron will generate an excitatory potential more quickly

solution.explanation: NCERT: the released neurotransmitters bind to their specific receptors on the post-synaptic membrane. This binding opens ion channels allowing the entry of ions, which can generate a new potential in the post-synaptic neuron. If the receptors are blocked, binding cannot occur, the channels do not open and no new potential arises.
steps: Transmitter release → binding to post-synaptic receptors → ion channels open → new potential
Receptors blocked → chain stops at binding
solution.why_others_wrong: A chemical synapse cannot switch to electrical transmission; the pre-synaptic neuron is unaffected; with receptors blocked no potential, excitatory or inhibitory, is produced.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Neural Control and Coordination', transmission of impulses
solution.final_answer: Option A: The neurotransmitters cannot bind and open ion channels, so no new potential is generated in the post-synaptic neuron
